original_anchor: This study examines whether annual financial trends, quarterly changes and management disclosures provide complementary information for predicting new episodes of corporate financial distress. The proposed multimodal attention network combines a Transformer, an LSTM and a Chinese financial language encoder. Three directional attention paths use financial summaries to query text and quarterly sequences; a sample-dependent gate aggregates the resulting representations. The analysis establishes a token-dependent attention cost, a conditional stability bound for convex aggregation, and the distinction between focal-loss reweighting and gradient allocation. The empirical design uses fixed prediction dates, a subsequent 12-month outcome window, chronological evaluation and matched fusion ablations. Re-examination of the available materials identifies unresolved sample provenance and inconsistencies in the reported metrics and figures. Consequently, the earlier performance estimates do not establish predictive superiority, semantic interpretability or earlier textual warning. The contribution at this stage is a corrected, testable model and evaluation design. Its potential use in corporate risk monitoring depends on completing the point-in-time dataset and obtaining reproducible out-of-time evidence.

original_comment: The mathematical bound holds for fixed vectors. It is not a proof of end-to-end robustness, causal attribution or interpretability of attention/gate weights.
original_anchor: Proof. Simplex weights define a convex combination; the triangle inequality gives both bounds. Changing an observation changes features as well as weights, so end-to-end stability needs additional bounds. Correlated vectors may yield the same output under different weights. Gate coefficients are therefore neither identified causal contributions nor automatically faithful explanations (Figure 3).
